{{Short description|Award for mathematical analysis work}}
[[File:Alfred_Ackermann-Teubner.jpg | thumb | right | alt=a black and white photo of a man in a suit looking at the camera  | Portrait of Alfred Ackermann-Teubner]]The '''Alfred Ackermann–Teubner Memorial Award for the Promotion of Mathematical Sciences''' recognized work in mathematical analysis.  It was established in 1912 by engineer Alfred Ackermann-Teubner and was an [[financial endowment|endowment]] of the [[University of Leipzig]].<ref>{{cite book |pages=348 |title=Constantin Carathéodory: Mathematics and Politics in Turbulent Times |last=Georgiadou |first= Maria |publisher=Springer |location=New York |isbn=3-540-20352-4 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IVIXBOFNty8C&pg=RA1-PA348&dq=%22Ackermann%E2%80%93Teubner+Memorial+Award%22 |year=2004}}</ref>

It was awarded 14 times between 1914 and 1941.<ref name="first">{{cite journal |journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |volume=21 |page=419 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1915-02671-6 |title=Notes |date=May 1915 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |location=Providence, Rhode Island |url=http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS/Repository/1.0/Disseminate?view=body&id=pdf_1&handle=euclid.bams/1183423213 |issue=8|doi-access=free }}</ref> Subsequent awards were to be made every other year until a surplus of 60,000 marks was accumulated within the [[financial endowment|endowment]], at which time, the prize was to be awarded annually. The subjects included:<ref>{{cite journal |page=157 |title=Notes and News |date=August–September 1912 |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |volume=19 |publisher=Mathematical Association of America  |jstor=2972758 |issue=8/9}}</ref>
* History, philosophy, teaching
* [[Mathematics]], especially [[arithmetic]] and [[algebra]]
* [[Mechanics]]
* [[Mathematical physics]]
* Mathematics, especially [[Mathematical analysis|analysis]]
* [[Astronomy]] and [[theory of errors]]
* Mathematics, especially [[geometry]]
* [[Applied mathematics]], especially [[geodesy]] and [[geophysics]].

== Honorees ==
The fifteen honorees between 1914 and 1941 are:<ref>[http://www.weiss-leipzig.de/ackermann-preis.htm Ackermann-Teubner memorial prize (Leipzig 1914-1941)]</ref>
* 1914: [[Felix Klein]]<ref name="first"/>
* 1916: [[Ernst Zermelo]], prize of 1,000 marks<ref>{{cite journal |journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |volume=23 |page=336 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1917-02963-1|title=Notes |date=April 1917 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |location=Providence, Rhode Island |url=http://www.projecteuclid.org/DPubS/Repository/1.0/Disseminate?view=body&id=pdf_1&handle=euclid.bams/1183424056 |issue=7|doi-access=free }}</ref>
* 1918: [[Ludwig Prandtl]]<ref>{{cite journal |journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |volume=25 |page= 477 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1919-03240-6|title=Notes |date=July 1919 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |location=Providence, Rhode Island |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ixkFAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA477&dq=Ackermann-Teubner+prize |author1=Society, American Mathematical|doi-access=free }}</ref>
* 1920: [[Gustav Mie]]<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|volume=27|number=5|pages=237–241|title=Notes|year=1921|url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.bams/1183425582|doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1921-03418-5|doi-access=free}}</ref> 
* 1922: [[Paul Koebe]]<ref>{{cite journal |journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |volume=29 |page=235 |title=Notes |date=May 1923 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |location=Providence, Rhode Island |url=http://www.projecteuclid.org/DPubS/Repository/1.0/Disseminate?view=body&id=pdf_1&handle=euclid.bams/1183485532 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1923-03715-4 |issue=5|doi-access=free }}</ref>
* 1924: [[Arnold Kohlschütter]]<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|volume=31|pages=375–378|title=Notes|year=1925|url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.bams/1183486570|issue=7|doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1925-04073-2|doi-access=free}}.</ref>
* 1926: [[Wilhelm Blaschke]]<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|volume=33|page=373|title=Notes|year=1927|url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.bams/1183492120|issue=3|doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1927-04389-0|doi-access=free}}.</ref>
* 1928: [[Albert Defant]]<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|volume=35|page=741|title=Notes|year=1929|url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.bams/1183493488|issue=5|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1929-04836-5 |doi-access=free}}.</ref>
* 1930: [[Johannes Tropfke]]
* 1932: [[Emmy Noether]] and [[Emil Artin]], co-honorees<ref>{{cite book |page=100 |title=Fifty Jewish women who changed the world |last=Felder  |first=D.G. |author2=Rosen, D. |publisher=Citadel Press |location=New York |isbn=0-8065-2656-4 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nUqo-_9mZ7sC&pg=PA100&dq=Ackermann-Teubner+Memorial |date=2005-02-01}}</ref>
* 1934: [[Erich Trefftz]]<sup>([[:de:Erich Trefftz|de]])</sup><ref>{{cite journal |journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |pages=178 | volume=41 |  doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1935-06071-9|title=Notes |date=May 1935 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |location=Providence, Rhode Island |url=https://www.ams.org/bull/1935-41-03/S0002-9904-1935-06071-9/S0002-9904-1935-06071-9.pdf|doi-access=free }}</ref>
* 1937: [[Pascual Jordan]]<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Jahresbericht der Deutschen Mathematiker-Vereinigung|editor=Teubner|title=Ackermann-Teubnerpreis 1937|year=1937|volume=47|page=76|
url=http://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/dms/load/img/?PPN=PPN37721857X_0047&DMDID=DMDLOG_0033&LOGID=LOG_0033&PHYSID=PHYS_0306}}.</ref>
* 1938: [[Erich Hecke]]<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Mathematische Annalen|pages=140|title=Ackermann-Teubnerpreis 1938|year=1940|publisher=Springer-Verlag|volume=117|issue=1|doi=10.1007/BF01450014}}.</ref>
* 1941: [[Paul ten Bruggencate]]<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Mathematische Annalen|volume=118|year=1941|page=440|url=http://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/dms/load/img/?PPN=PPN235181684_0118&DMDID=DMDLOG_0031|title=Alfred Ackermann-Teubner Gedächnispreis|doi=10.1007/bf01487379}}</ref>

== Jurists ==
In 1937, [[Constantin Carathéodory]] and [[Erhard Schmidt]] were invited to jury the award.<ref>Georgiadou, p. 348</ref>  Along with [[Wilhelm Blaschke]], Carathéodory was invited again in 1944 by the German Union of Mathematicians.<ref>Georgiadou, p. 399</ref>
